text: A handler that sleeps 300 ms delayed the next event by 300 ms. What does that look like to a user of a real application?
choices: The toolkit spawns a second dispatch thread to keep the interface alive.
Events queue up and are then delivered faster to catch up, so nothing is noticeable.
Only the control that was clicked becomes unresponsive; the rest of the window still works.
The whole interface freezes — nothing repaints and no button responds, because repaint is an event too.
explanation: There is one loop, and it is inside your handler. Every unresponsive application you have used was a handler that took too long. Anything over about 100 ms is noticeable and anything over a second reads as broken; the blocking operations are file reads, network requests, database queries, sleeps, large loops, and waiting for a lock.
